eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus centers on 28–29°C as Shanghai’s peak temperature for August 13 because current model guidance and observational trends point to widespread cloud cover and scattered thundershowers that reduce incoming solar radiation and promote evaporative cooling. August climatology favors highs near 31–32°C, yet persistent moisture from the East Asian monsoon and an approaching weak disturbance are expected to cap daytime heating, keeping surface temperatures 2–4°C below seasonal norms. Official forecasts from agencies such as the China Meteorological Administration and global ensembles show a tight cluster between 28°C and 31°C, with limited upside risk from clearing skies or stronger insolation. The narrow distribution of market-implied probabilities around these two outcomes reflects high confidence in the rain-cooled scenario, while lower odds for 30°C or above account for the small chance of model shifts toward drier conditions before the daily maximum is recorded.
